summary: Former Manchester City player Cole Palmer scored a penalty in the fifth minute of stoppage time to give Chelsea a 4-4 draw with Premier League champions Manchester City at Stamford Bridge, after City had come from behind or been pegged back repeatedly. Liverpool beat Brentford 3-0 with two goals from Mohamed Salah, moving into second on 27 points. The article also covers manager reactions from Mauricio Pochettino and Pep Guardiola and other weekend results.
one_line: Cole Palmer's stoppage-time penalty earned Chelsea a 4-4 draw with Manchester City, while Salah's double lifted Liverpool to second with a 3-0 win over Brentford.
key_facts: Cole Palmer scored a penalty in the fifth minute of stoppage time to give Chelsea a 4-4 draw with Manchester City at Stamford Bridge.
Palmer left Manchester City for Chelsea in September in a deal worth around $A82 million.
Rodri's deflected effort off Thiago Silva put City 4-3 up with four minutes of regulation time left, before referee Anthony Taylor awarded a penalty when Ruben Dias fouled substitute Armando Broja.
Erling Haaland scored twice for City, including a 25th-minute penalty, and reached 13 Premier League goals this season.
Chelsea's goals came from Thiago Silva (header from Conor Gallagher's corner), Raheem Sterling (37th minute), Nicolas Jackson (67th) and Palmer's penalty.
Manuel Akanji headed in Bernardo Silva's cross in first-half stoppage time to make it 2-2.
City lead the table on 28 points, Liverpool are second on 27 above Arsenal on goal difference, and Tottenham are fourth on 26 after successive defeats.
Mauricio Pochettino apologised for his touchline behaviour, saying he was emotional, and praised his players for never giving up.
Pep Guardiola called the 4-4 a fair result and said City went into the international break top of the league, which he did not expect after the Arsenal defeat.
Mohamed Salah scored twice in Liverpool's 3-0 win over Brentford, reaching his 200th goal in English football and 10 Premier League goals this season, scoring in a sixth successive home game.
Diogo Jota scored a late goal for Liverpool, ending questions after the draw at Luton and Europa League defeat in Toulouse.
Aston Villa beat Fulham 3-1 to move fifth, West Ham beat Nottingham Forest 3-2 with a late Tomas Soucek winner, and Sheffield United drew 1-1 at Brighton to leave the bottom.
